title: Changes Around Us: Physical and Chemical

topics.title: A substance may change in appearance but remain the same

concepts.learning_objective: Identify a physical change as one in which only physical properties such as shape and size change and no new substance is formed.
Explain why changes of state such as melting and boiling of water are physical changes.

topics.title: A substance may change in appearance and not remain the same

concepts.learning_objective: Identify a chemical change as one in which one or more new substances are formed through a chemical reaction.
Use the turning of lime water milky as a test for carbon dioxide and interpret the reaction involved.
Explain why rusting of iron is a chemical change that forms iron oxide.
Describe combustion as a reaction with oxygen that gives out heat and/or light, and identify combustible substances.
Define ignition temperature and use it to explain why a substance does or does not catch fire.
State the three requirements for combustion and apply them to putting out a fire.

topics.title: Physical and chemical changes in the same process

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish the physical and chemical changes that take place when a candle burns.
Classify everyday processes as physical, chemical, or involving both kinds of change.
Distinguish changes that can be reversed from those that cannot be reversed.
Evaluate whether a change is desirable or undesirable in a given situation, including its effect on the environment.
Explain weathering of rocks as a combination of physical and chemical changes that leads to soil formation.
Describe erosion as the movement of rock pieces, soil and sediments by wind and flowing water.
